audit.why: Even lane (49.33% WR, 373 games): Mel controls early with range and W reflect, Azir takes over from first item onward. Difficulty 5.5/10 fits.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart shows 'Skill' on all seven rows while the packet and content layer both say Mel 1-5, Azir first item onward; phases[5-6].why also describe Mel winning stages the content gives to Azir.
audit.why: Packet levelChart and content win[] agree: Mel through level 6, Azir at first item and 2+ items. Azir's Nashor's/soldier spike outranges Mel's poke.
audit.corrected: phases[0-4].side -> Mel, phases[5-6].side -> Azir with matching whys and ratings; win[] already correct so no content edits needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns has no numbers; Azir's E shield absorbing Mel's burst (missingInteractions) is nowhere on the page; dontsFull[2] body is pasted tradeBad and never answers its own title about non-projectiles.
audit.why: Azir E Shifting Sands is 22s at rank 1 and shields him — the decisive cooldown. Emperor's Divide is a soldier wall, not a projectile, so Mel's W Rebuttal does not answer it.
audit.corrected: Cooldown numbers added; E-shield-eats-burst stated; dontsFull[2].d now names Divide as the non-projectile.

edits.before: Luden's spike: snare-volley chunks half bars and the execute cleans the remainder. Force contacts.
edits.after: His Nashor's spike: stacked soldiers out-range and out-DPS your volleys. Poke only when his E is down.

edits.before: Late Mel is a counter-artillery battery: reflect their poke, snare their dive, and execute the chipped.
edits.after: Full-stack Azir with Emperor's Divide is a top-tier teamfight mid — stay behind your front line and W his procs.

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. It governs your forward steps. - W Rebuttal spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — the shield-dash is down 22s at rank 1, and its shield eats your burst, so force it before you commit. - Q Conquering Sands is 14s early — poke inside that gap. - W Rebuttal spent on poke is a death you scheduled.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: His Q Conquering Sands runs a 14s cooldown at rank 1 — once he repositions soldiers, volley his next last-hit for free stacks.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Emperor's Divide is a charging soldier wall, not a projectile — Rebuttal will not reflect it, and it knocks you clean out of your own all-in.

edits.before: Azir wins by landing Shifting Sands, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Azir wins by stacking soldiers, poking with Q from outside your answer, and walling your all-in with Divide.

notes: Content win[] and whys[] were already correct (Mel 1-5, Azir from first item), so side edits are unpaired by design per the chart rule. Did not assert whether Mel's W Rebuttal reflects Azir soldier attacks — the Yasuo Wind Wall precedent suggests soldier stabs are projectiles, but the kit files cannot confirm reflect eligibility, so the page stays silent on it. Packet suspectName 'Land Emperor's Divide' is a false positive — Emperor's Divide is the real R name.
